overview: Kiribati is an island country in the central Pacific, made up of 33 atolls and islands spread across a huge area of ocean. Its capital is South Tarawa. Kiribati became independent from the United Kingdom in 1979. Its Line Islands are in the world's earliest time zone, so they are among the first places on Earth to see each new day.

geography.text: Kiribati's islands lie in three groups, the Gilbert, Phoenix and Line Islands, scattered across the equator over thousands of kilometres of ocean. Almost all are low coral atolls only a few metres above sea level, which makes the country very vulnerable to rising seas. Banaba is the only raised island.

history.text: The Gilbert Islands were settled by Micronesian people. Britain made them a protectorate in 1892, together with the Ellice Islands, today Tuvalu. The Battle of Tarawa in 1943 was one of the bloodiest of the Pacific War. Kiribati became independent in 1979, and in 1995 it moved the International Date Line so that the whole country shares the same day.

events.title: British protectorate
events.text: Britain takes control of the Gilbert and Ellice Islands.

events.title: Battle of Tarawa
events.text: US forces capture Tarawa from Japan after fierce fighting.

events.title: Date line moved
events.text: Kiribati moves the date line so all its islands share one date.
